text:
NextItNet uses causal dilated convolutions and residual connections to access longer histories. Architectural reach does not establish learned influence: effective receptive fields can occupy only part of the theoretical receptive field. Compute accessibility from the actual convolution stack, then measure influence separately; gradient magnitude alone does not establish causal usefulness. Sources: [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf), [effective receptive fields](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.04128).

Activation-patching research shows that corruption choice, intervention direction and output metric can change localization conclusions. Proposed NextItNet adaptation: freeze the single trained model, cache clean activations, corrupt selected nonpadding history positions, and restore individual convolution-branch outputs or residual states. Also replace clean activations with corrupted counterparts; restoration and destruction provide complementary evidence, conditional on the intervention. For h′=h+F(h), zeroing F(h) tests the residual branch while retaining the identity path; replacing h′ tests a broader intervention. Preserve left padding, final-nonpadding readout, candidate identities and eligibility. Measure target–competitor score margins, target rank and HR@10 changes; compare individual and joint interventions because interacting paths can hide effects. Sources: [patching methodology](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042), [interpretation guidance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255). These are proposed adaptations, not established NextItNet findings.

Attribution sanity checks ask whether explanations depend on learned parameters. Progressively randomize layers in temporary diagnostic copies and compare attribution maps with the trained model; persistent similarity undermines claims about learned influence. Separately test faithfulness by comparing attribution rankings with measured intervention effects and random-selection controls. Passing randomization checks alone does not establish faithfulness. Keep diagnostic copies out of prediction and restore the original checkpoint. Source: [Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03292).
